title: Second Spanish Republic
capsule: The Second Spanish Republic was proclaimed on April 14, 1931, following King Alfonso XIII's departure from Spain, and established a parliamentary democratic system with a secular constitution promulgated in December 1931. The republic undertook land reform, anticlerical legislation, and regional autonomy statutes for Catalonia and the Basque Country, generating intense political polarization between left and right. General Francisco Franco's military uprising on July 17–18, 1936 triggered the Spanish Civil War; with decisive material support from Nazi Germany and Fascist Italy, Nationalist forces entered Madrid on March 28, 1939, ending the Republic. The legitimate republican government survived in exile until 1977.
attestation: Boundaries from Seshat Cliopatria (Bennett et al., Scientific Data 2025; CC BY 4.0), digitized from standard historical atlases at ~0.07° resolution. The Second Republic's territorial extent is well attested; it controlled peninsular Spain and the Canary Islands, with the Nationalist zone expanding progressively from mid-1936 onward as documented in detailed campaign records.
